title: The Borrowed Name
brief: YOUR MISSION: A new post assigns an Itbayat image to Lantern Six. Compare similar vessel names, camera time and independent position records. File three supported findings without merging different vessels or mistaking an archive time for a capture time.
disclaimer: FICTIONAL SCENARIO / REAL GEOGRAPHY. All vessels, records and observations are invented. Timeline times are UTC; the image's clock convention is evidence to investigate. Natural Earth coastlines are generalized. Not for navigation.

evidence.title: 01 / Review request
evidence.body:
15 September 2026 / 09:10 UTC

Yesterday's tracking-gap review is closed. Today a circulating post identifies a vessel in an Itbayat image as Lantern Six and calls the image time 08:20 UTC.

Your assignment:
1. Identify which registered vessel best matches the visible structural features.
2. Find when camera Q4 TOOK the image, expressed in UTC. Read the camera display in record 03, find that camera's clock convention in record 04, then convert the display to UTC. Do not use the time when the archive processed the image.
3. Reconcile the independently recorded vessel positions.

Pin useful records, then tick their citation boxes separately under each finding. Submitting alone does not finish the case: all three findings must say SUPPORTED in the same submission.

Do not assume a shared name identifies a hull. An image, its archive entry and a repost of that image are not three independent sightings. Every record needed for this review is available on this desk.

evidence.title: 02 / Local vessel register
evidence.body:
Register extract / 15 September 2026, 06:00 UTC
These fictional local identifiers are not IMO numbers.

LANTERN SIX / LN-6
Cabin side: three rectangular windows in one row.
Stern marking: one horizontal bar below the vessel name.

LANTERN NINE / LN-9
Cabin side: two round portholes.
Stern marking: two horizontal bars below the vessel name.

Both names begin LANTERN. Cropped name lettering alone does not distinguish them. Structural descriptions apply to this authored scenario; they are not general vessel-identification rules.

evidence.title: 03 / Camera image and archive entry
evidence.body:
CAMERA DISPLAY / WHEN THE IMAGE WAS TAKEN
15 SEP 2026 / 08:20
No time zone is printed on the image. Read record 04, Q4 camera setting card, to establish what clock Q4 uses before converting this reading to UTC.

ARCHIVE PROCESSING / WHEN THE FILE WAS INDEXED
15 September 2026 / 08:45 UTC
This is when the archive processed the file, NOT when the camera took the image. It is already UTC; it is not the input to the capture-time conversion.

Frame reference: Q4-0915-0820
Camera identifier: Q4
Location tag: Itbayat service approach

Observation transcript:
The name begins LANTERN; the remainder is cropped. The local hull number is unreadable. The cabin side has two round portholes. Two horizontal bars are visible below the cropped stern name. No cargo detail can be established.

This is an authored text observation, NOT a supplied photograph. No pixel enhancement or external image research is required.

evidence.title: 04 / Q4 camera setting card
evidence.body:
CAMERA Q4 CLOCK CONVENTION
Applies throughout 15 September; no clock reset or measured drift is recorded.

Q4's image display uses PHILIPPINE LOCAL TIME: UTC+08:00. This clock is eight hours AHEAD of UTC. Record 03 does not print a zone on the image; this setting card establishes it.

CONVERSION
Take the CAMERA DISPLAY from record 03 and subtract eight hours to obtain UTC. Check whether the subtraction changes the calendar date. For example, 14:00 local is 06:00 UTC on the same date.

Do not subtract from the archive's processing time: that timestamp is already UTC and describes a different event. The archive does not rewrite the camera display.

ADMINISTRATIVE TIMESTAMP
This setting card was copied at 08:50 UTC on 15 September. That is not the image capture time.

evidence.title: 05 / Itbayat approach ledger
evidence.body:
Ledger filed: 15 September 2026, 00:35 UTC
Approach observation: 00:10 UTC
Vessel: LANTERN NINE / clear local identifier LN-9
Approximate offshore approach: 20.760 N, 121.775 E

A shore clerk records LN-9 approaching the Itbayat service area. The clerk kept this ledger independently of camera Q4. The record does not identify LN-6 and does not give LN-9's full route.

The arrival observation and this ledger's later filing time are different events.

evidence.title: 06 / Basco shore observation
evidence.body:
15 September 2026 / 06:40 UTC
Location: offshore near Basco, Batan Island
Approximate observation: 20.480 N, 121.960 E
Vessel: LANTERN SIX / clear local identifier LN-6
Cabin side: three rectangular windows.

The observer records this vessel near Basco at this time. The note was kept independently of the Itbayat desk and camera archive. It establishes a position observation, not every movement before or after it. It does not prove LN-6 never visited another island.

evidence.title: 07 / Circulating identification post
evidence.body:
Posted 15 September 2026, 09:00 UTC
Attached archive frame: Q4-0915-0820

'The cropped name says LANTERN, so this is Lantern Six at Itbayat at 08:20 UTC today. Together with the Basco report, this proves its northbound run.'

The attachment is a copy of the indexed archive frame, not a separate observation. The post provides no additional clear hull number, camera setting record or independent Itbayat position fix. Test the identification and time convention against the original records; do not count the copy as corroboration.

findings.question: 1. Which vessel best matches the image?

options.label: Both names identify the same hull

findings.explanation: The register distinguishes two hulls. Two round cabin portholes and two stern bars in the transcript match LN-9, not LN-6's three rectangular windows and single bar. The cropped shared name alone is insufficient.

findings.question: 2. When did camera Q4 take the image, in UTC (not archive processing time)?
findings.explanation: Use two records: 03 supplies the camera display, 08:20 on 15 September; 04 establishes that Q4 uses Philippine local time, UTC+08:00. Local time is eight hours ahead of UTC, so 08:20 minus eight hours is 00:20 UTC on 15 September. The 08:45 timestamp describes archive processing, a different event; the 08:50 timestamp describes copying the setting card. Neither is when the image was taken.

findings.question: 3. What do independent position records establish?

options.label: Both positions form one LN-6 track
LN-9 at Itbayat; LN-6 near Basco

findings.explanation: The independent Itbayat ledger identifies LN-9 at 00:10 UTC; the Basco observer identifies LN-6 at 06:40 UTC. These are different vessels, not a single observed track. Together with the image and clock comparison, they undermine the post's conflation. They do not reconstruct either vessel's entire day or prove LN-6 never visited Itbayat.

hints: Finding 1 / identity: compare record 02's registered windows and stern bars with record 03's observation. The shared word LANTERN is not enough. Pin both records and cite them under finding 1.

Finding 2 / choose the event: record 03 contains a camera display (08:20) and archive processing time (08:45 UTC). The question asks when the camera TOOK the image, not when the archive processed it. Start with 08:20; its clock convention comes from record 04.

Finding 2 / convert and cite: record 04 says Q4 uses Philippine local time, UTC+08:00, eight hours AHEAD of UTC. Subtract eight hours from the 08:20 camera display and check the date. Pin records 03 and 04, then tick BOTH under finding 2; pinning alone is not citation.

Finding 3 / independent positions: compare the clear local IDs in records 05 and 06. Different hulls must not become one route. After submitting, fix every finding that is not SUPPORTED: change a REVISE answer, or add the listed citations for NEEDS SUPPORT, then Submit again.
